sanskrit: veda vai te takman nāma viśvaso nāma vā asi | asamaratho nāma te pitā hārṣī nāma takman te mātā śimidā nāma te svasā ||
english: I know your name, O Takman — you are also called Viśvasa. Asamaratha is your father's name, O Takman; Hārṣī is your mother's name; Śimidā is the name of your sister.

sanskrit: giriṃ gaccheti sāptamikī ||
english: "Go to the mountain" — this is the verse belonging to the seventh-day fever charm.

sanskrit: asurās tvod ava bharan samudrād adhi māyayā | tad āsrāvasya bheṣajaṃ tad u rogam anīnaśat ||
english: The Asuras bore you down from the ocean by their magic. That remedy for the flux — that same thing destroyed the disease.

sanskrit: rogasthānam asṛksthānam atho āsrāvabheṣajam | babhror aśvasya vāreṇ- -āpi nahyāmi tā aham ||
english: The seat of disease, the seat of blood-flow, and likewise the remedy for the flux — I bind all those up with the tail-hair of the brown horse.

sanskrit: yan me daṇḍo vāpāti dīkṣayā tapasā saha | tam ahaṃ punar ā dade punar indraḥ punar bhagaḥ | punar me brahmaṇaspatir brahma jīvitavā adāt ||
english: Whatever staff of mine fell away together with consecration and austerity — that I take up again. Indra restores it, Bhaga restores it; Brahmaṇaspati has again given me the brahman power so that I may live.

sanskrit: itthād ulūkāpa tanvan uttānapādam arbhakaḥ | sa me premāṇam ā vahad apa dveṣaḥ parā vahat ||
english: In this manner, the little one lying face-upward, stretching out like an owl — may he bring love to me and carry hatred far away.

sanskrit: yathā bāṇaḥ susaṃśitaḥ parāpataty āśumat | evā mūtrasya te dhārā parā patati ketumat ||
english: Just as a well-whetted arrow flies swiftly away, so may your stream of urine fly forth brightly and freely.

sanskrit: yathā madhu madhukṛtaḥ saṃbharanti madhāv adhi | evā me madhumad vaco deveṣu puruṣeṣu ca ||
english: Just as the bees gather honey upon the honeycomb, so may my honeyed speech be sweet among the gods and among people.

sanskrit: dīrghāyutvāya tapase mahyā ariṣṭatātaye | suparṇo mahyam abravīd etad utsaktabheṣajam etat puliśabheṣajam ||
english: For long life, for austerity, for my wholeness and safety, the Suparṇa (eagle) spoke to me: this is the Utsakta remedy, this is the Puliśa remedy.

sanskrit: agnī rakṣāṃsīty ekā ||
english: "Agni drives away the demons" — this is a single verse (a one-verse charm).

sanskrit: paiśir mātā peśiḥ pitā paiśeyaḥ peśyā hataḥ | addhā kṛtasya brahmaṇā vṛścikasyārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: Paiśī is the mother, Peśa is the father; the Paiśeya — born of Peśa — is slain. Truly, by brahman power already wielded, the scorpion's venom is made powerless.

sanskrit: nir hvayāmi parṇasādān nir ut pucchād u te viṣam | bhūmis ta ucyate mātā tasyai te nama it sṛja ||
english: I call out the leaf-sitters; I draw out your venom from the tail. The Earth is declared your mother — release your venom as homage to her.

sanskrit: kim u danta āmayati kim abhūd upaveśanam | āpo nir asyatā krimim agade kṛṇutā hanū ||
english: What does the tooth ache with? What was the cause of the sitting-down in pain? Waters, drive out the worm; make the jaws free of poison.

sanskrit: yatra bhūmyā anāmṛtaṃ divi candramasi śritam | vidvām̐ ahaṃ tatra manye māhaṃ pautram aghaṃ ni gām ||
english: Where the immortality of the Earth rests in heaven, in the moon — knowing that place, I direct my mind there. May I not bring harm upon my grandson.

sanskrit: yat te susīme hṛdayam ado vai tat prajāpatau | vedāma tasya te vayaṃ (māhaṃ pautram aghaṃ ni gām) ||
english: O Susīmā, your heart — that truly resides in Prajāpati. We know that heart of yours. May I not bring harm upon my grandson.

sanskrit: yat suvarṇāyā hṛdayaṃ pṛthivyām adhi niṣṭhitam | vedāhaṃ tasyās tan nāma (māhaṃ pautram aghaṃ ni gām) ||
english: The heart of Suvarṇā, firmly established upon the earth — I know that name of hers. May I not bring harm upon my grandson.

sanskrit: agner hṛdayam asi vidyut tat tvā tathā veda | māhaṃ pautram aghaṃ ni gām ||
english: You are the heart of Agni; lightning — thus I know you as such. May I not bring harm upon my grandson.

sanskrit: prajā ime prajāpata indrāgnī śarma yacchatam | yathāhaṃ jyog ihāsāni prajānām adhipā vaśī ||
english: These creatures are yours, O Prajāpati; may Indra and Agni grant them shelter. So that I may dwell here long as master and ruler over the people.

sanskrit: yāṃ prajām avidām ady- -ātmanaḥ parinirmitām | āyuṣmatīṃ tanūkṛtāṃ tām̐ agne jarase naya ||
english: The offspring that I have found today, born from myself, full of vitality and with a body well-made — lead them, O Agni, to old age.

sanskrit: indra ivāsāni sāsahir agnir iva jyotiṣā bṛhan | sūrya iva viśvataḥ pratyak samudra iva duṣṭaraḥ ||
english: May I be a conqueror like Indra, great in radiance like Agni, shining in all directions like the Sun, and like the ocean — hard to cross.

sanskrit: ṛcaṃ sāma yad aprākṣaṃ havir ojo yajur balam | etaṃ mā tasmān mā hiṃsīd vedaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ śacīpate ||
english: The Ṛc, the Sāman, the oblation and vital power, the Yajus and strength — whatever of these I have asked about: from that wrong, O lord of Śacī, may the questioned Veda not harm me.

sanskrit: ud bhare dyāvāpṛthivī sahauṣadhībhiḥ | gṛhṇāmi prajāṃ nir apaḥ sṛjāmi ||
english: I lift up Heaven and Earth together with the plants. I take hold of offspring; I release the waters.

sanskrit: mā na āpo medhāṃ mā brahma pra mathiṣṭana | suṣyadā yūyaṃ syandadhvam upahūto 'haṃ sumedhā varcasvī ||
english: O Waters, do not shake out of us our mental power, do not shake out the brahman. You flow as nourishers — I am called forth as one of fine intelligence and full of radiant power.

sanskrit: mā no medhāṃ mā no dīkṣāṃ mā no hiṃsiṣṭa yat tapaḥ | śivā naḥ sarva āyuṣa āpo bhavantu mātaraḥ ||
english: Do not injure our mental power, do not injure our consecration, do not injure our austerity. May the Waters be our auspicious mothers through all our span of life.

sanskrit: iha prajā viśvarūpā ramantām asmin goṣṭhe viśvabhṛto janitrīḥ | agniṃ kulāyam upa saṃviśantīr jānantu naḥ payasā ghṛtena ||
english: May offspring of all forms take delight here; may the all-sustaining mothers in this cattle-stall, entering around the home-fire, know us with milk and with ghee.

sanskrit: rantaya stha ramataya stha mayi śrita stha mayi śrayadhvam | manotā nāma stha grāmyā apsaraso veda vo vittam ā mā viśata ||
english: You are sources of joy, you are sources of delight; you rest in me, lean upon me. You are called Manotā — village Apsarases; I know you, I understand you — enter into me.

sanskrit: śarva nīlaśikhaṇḍa vīra karmaṇikarmaṇi | imām asya prāśaṃ jahi yenedaṃ vivadāmahe ||
english: O Śarva, blue-crested hero, in every act and deed — strike down this man's boasting, by reason of which we are in dispute with him.

sanskrit: tṛtīyakaṃ vitṛtīyaṃ sadandiṃ takmānam uta rājayakṣmam | yathā śakra unmumoca tṛtīyakam evāhaṃ tad un muñcāmi tṛtīyakaṃ tam asyām oṣadhyāṃ badhnāmi ||
english: The tertian fever, the non-tertian, the continual fever, the Takman, and also the royal consumption — as mighty Śakra released the tertian fever, so I release it; I bind that tertian fever in this plant.

sanskrit: ādhvastapakṣṇe bṛhate pathe 'ham akaraṃ namaḥ ||
english: To the great road with its wings outstretched I have made obeisance.

sanskrit: indrāya tviṣīmate pathe 'ham akaraṃ namaḥ ||
english: To Indra, to the glittering road I have made obeisance.
